references.text: The preceding verse introduces the rule about the right of redemption for houses in walled cities, which verse 30 continues to elaborate on with a time limit of one year.
A contrasting provision regarding houses in unwalled villages, which are to be regarded as open fields and can be redeemed and released in the Jubilee year, unlike houses in walled cities.
The fundamental Jubilee provision stating that property shall be returned, though verse 30 constitutes an exception for city houses.
The principle that the land belongs to the Lord and cannot be sold permanently, from which city houses in verse 30 are an exception.
Provisions concerning the consecration and redemption of landed property in relation to the Jubilee year, reflecting similar principles regarding permanent transfer of property.
Ruth deals with the right of redemption (goel) for property, the same theme of redemption addressed in Leviticus 25:30.
Jeremiah exercises the right of redemption to buy back family land, illustrating the practice described in Leviticus 25.
